ei.title: The Science Behind the Mona Lisa
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
The Science Behind the Mona Lisa

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is ①<u>known</u> as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an ②<u>accomplished</u> scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not ③<u>perceiving</u> as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as ④<u>informing</u> upon the other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 예술과 과학은 상호 배타적인 것으로 인식되지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①known: is known as — 수동태 정상

✅ ②accomplished: 형용사(뛰어난) 정상

❌ ③perceiving → perceived: were not perceived as — 수동태 구문에서 과거분사 필요 ←정답

✅ ④informing: was seen as informing — 전치사 as 뒤 동명사 정상
det.tip: be perceived as = ~으로 인식되다. 수동태(be + p.p.)이므로 perceived가 맞다.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was ①<u>fascinated</u> by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to ②<u>determine</u> the origin of nerves that ③<u>control</u> each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy ④<u>allowing</u> him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 해부학에 대한 관심이 그가 모나리자의 신비로운 미소를 만들어내게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①fascinated: was fascinated by — 감정 수동태 정상

✅ ②determine: to determine — to부정사 정상

✅ ③control: nerves that control — 관계대명사절 동사(복수) 정상

❌ ④allowing → allowed: 주어 This interest에 대한 본동사가 필요하므로 과거형 allowed ←정답
det.tip: This interest(주어) + allowed(본동사). 분사(allowing)는 본동사가 될 수 없다.

questions.passage: In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for ①<u>which</u> he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting ②<u>utilizes</u> da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is ③<u>slight</u> turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes are looking at us, even when we are not ④<u>directly</u> in front of the painting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 각 요소가 약간 돌려져 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①which: for which he is famous — 전치사+관계대명사 정상

✅ ②utilizes: This painting(3인칭 단수)에 동사 정상

❌ ③slight → slightly: 과거분사 turned를 수식하는 부사 필요 ←정답

✅ ④directly: 부사(직접적으로) 정상
det.tip: slightly(부사)가 turned(분사)를 수식. slight(형용사)는 동사/분사 수식 불가.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art ①<u>that</u> da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his ②<u>magnificent</u> artistic skills. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still ③<u>facing</u> the viewer. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The ④<u>farther</u> the object is, the smaller the scale.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 눈은 여전히 관람자를 향한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①that: It was ~ that 강조구문 정상

✅ ②magnificent: 형용사(웅장한) 정상

❌ ③facing → face: while절에서 the eyes still face — 주어+동사 구조, still 뒤에 동사원형 필요 ←정답

✅ ④farther: the farther ~ the smaller — 비교급 상관구문 정상
det.tip: while the eyes still face the viewer: still + 동사원형. facing(분사)은 주어 eyes의 본동사 역할 불가.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most ①<u>intelligent</u> painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an ②<u>amateur</u> scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually ③<u>exclusive</u>. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the ④<u>outstanding</u> masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 다빈치는 뛰어난(accomplished) 과학자였다. amateur(아마추어)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ①intelligent(지능이 뛰어난) — 원문 그대로 적절

❌ ②amateur(아마추어의) — 원문은 accomplished(뛰어난). 예술적 걸작을 만들 정도의 과학자를 아마추어라 하는 것은 부적절 ←정답

✅ ③exclusive(배타적인) — 원문 그대로 적절

✅ ④outstanding(뛰어난) — 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: accomplished(뛰어난/숙련된) ↔ amateur(아마추어의/미숙한). 문맥상 뛰어난 과학자.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's ①<u>mysterious</u> smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes are ②<u>staring</u> straight out. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of ③<u>depth</u> in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the ④<u>more</u> detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 물체가 멀수록 윤곽이 덜(less) 상세하다. more(더)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ①mysterious(신비로운) — 원문 그대로 적절

✅ ②staring(응시하는) — 원문 그대로 적절

✅ ③depth(깊이) — 원문 그대로 적절

❌ ④more(더) — 원문은 less(덜). 물체가 멀수록 윤곽이 덜 상세해진다는 맥락에서 more는 반대 ←정답
det.tip: the less detailed the outlines: 멀수록 덜 상세. less ↔ more.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.
questions.stem: 다빈치는 예술적 걸작으로 가장 잘 알려져 있지만 뛰어난 과학자이기도 했다.

det.korean: 예술적 걸작으로 유명하지만 뛰어난 과학자이기도 했다 — 참(T).
det.analysis: ✅ T: 'Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist.' — 원문과 일치.
det.tip: accomplished = 뛰어난/숙련된. best known for = ~으로 가장 잘 알려진.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 다빈치는 미소가 형성되기 시작하는 방식에는 관심이 없었다.

det.korean: 다빈치는 미소 형성에 매료되었다 — 거짓(F).
det.analysis: ❌ F: 'Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form.' — fascinated(매료된)이므로 관심이 없었다는 것은 거짓.
det.tip: fascinated by = ~에 매료된. 관심이 없었다는 진술과 반대.

questions.passage: He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting.
questions.stem: 다빈치는 몸통, 머리, 눈을 각 요소가 약간 돌아가도록 세심하게 배치했다.

det.korean: 세심하게 배치하여 각 요소가 약간 돌아가 있다 — 참(T).
det.analysis: ✅ T: 'He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned' — 원문과 일치.
det.tip: carefully positioned = 세심하게 배치했다. slightly turned = 약간 돌려져 있는.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as __________ exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 예술과 과학은 상호(mutually) 배타적으로 인식되지 않았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①partially(부분적으로) — exclusive 앞 수식어로 맥락 부적합

❌ ②barely(간신히) — 맥락과 무관

❌ ③strictly(엄격히) — 배타적 의미와 호응하나 원문과 불일치

✅ ④mutually(상호적으로) — mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인) 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: mutually exclusive = 상호 배타적인. Rather 이하에서 서로 영향을 준다고 함.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in __________ allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 해부학(anatomy)에 대한 관심이 미소를 표현하게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①anatomy(해부학) — 얼굴 근육과 신경의 기원을 연구한 맥락과 일치 ←정답

❌ ②astronomy(천문학) — 얼굴 근육 연구와 무관

❌ ③geometry(기하학) — 미소 형성 과정과 직접 무관

❌ ④philosophy(철학) — 신경/근육 탐구와 무관
det.tip: anatomy = 해부학. 얼굴 근육과 신경을 연구한 것이 단서.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 르네상스 시대에 예술과 과학은 완전히 분리되어 있었다
다빈치는 과학적 접근을 통해 뛰어난 걸작을 만들었다

det.korean: 과학적 접근을 통해 걸작을 만들었다 — 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ①예술가로만 알려진 것이 아님 — accomplished scientist이기도 함

❌ ②완전히 분리된 것이 아님 — not perceived as mutually exclusive

✅ ③'it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces' — 일치 ←정답

❌ ④유일한 작품이 아님 — One example is the Mona Lisa(하나의 예)
det.tip: through a scientific approach to art = 예술에 대한 과학적 접근을 통해.

questions.passage: He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 다빈치는 몸통, 머리, 눈을 세심하게 배치했다
그림에서 물체가 멀수록 색이 더 선명해진다
모나리자의 눈은 정면이 아닌 곳에서도 바라보는 것처럼 느껴진다

det.korean: 물체가 멀수록 색이 더 미묘해진다(subtle) — 선명해진다는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ①세심한 배치 — 'carefully positioned' 일치

❌ ②물체가 멀수록 색이 선명 — 'the more subtle the colors' = 더 미묘함. 선명해진다는 반대 ←정답

✅ ③정면 아닌 곳에서도 바라보는 느낌 — 'even when we are not directly in front' 일치

✅ ④깊이의 착각 — 'created the illusion of depth' 일치
det.tip: subtle = 미묘한. 멀수록 더 subtle(미묘) ≠ 더 선명.

det.korean: 물체가 멀수록 규모가 더 작아진다(smaller). larger는 틀림.
det.analysis:

❌ ④the larger the scale → the smaller the scale: 원문은 물체가 멀수록 규모가 더 작아진다(smaller) ←정답
det.tip: the farther ~ the smaller: 멀수록 작아진다. larger(더 큰)은 원문과 반대.

det.tip: The Science Behind the Mona Lisa = 모나리자 뒤에 숨겨진 과학.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 다빈치는 과학적 지식을 활용하여 모나리자의 다양한 효과를 만들었다

det.korean: 과학적 지식 활용 → 미소, 시선, 깊이감 등 다양한 효과.
det.analysis:
❌ ①우연이 아님 — 해부학 연구와 세심한 배치의 결과

❌ ②색채가 가장 중요하다는 내용 없음 — 색은 깊이감의 한 요소일 뿐

❌ ③해부학이 미술과 무관하다는 것은 본문과 반대

✅ ④해부학(미소) + 배치(시선) + 깊이감(원근법) = 과학적 지식의 다양한 활용 ←정답
det.tip: anatomy(미소), positioning(시선), illusion of depth(깊이) — 세 가지 과학적 기법.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 들어갈 영어를 쓰시오.

"하나가 다른 하나에 영향을 미치는 것으로 여겨졌다."

[조건] (1) as, informing, other, the, upon을 모두 사용할 것 (2) 5단어로 쓸 것 (5단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 다른 하나에 영향을 미치는 것으로(as informing upon the other).
det.analysis: ✅ 'one was seen as informing upon the other' — seen as 뒤 동명사구. informing upon = ~에 영향을 미치다. 5단어 일치.
det.tip: be seen as + V-ing = ~하는 것으로 여겨지다. inform upon = ~에 영향을 미치다.
